title: Needs you
how: Only what is open for you, oldest first. Each item says what to do, links everything it needs, and gives my recommendation. It leaves this page once you have answered it here or done it.
Pick an answer under each item; a note is optional.
foot: One page, one link, kept current (his order of 2 November). The same list is kept as plain data beside it (items.json) for the advisor's checker.

sections.name: Next week's order (16 to 23 November), built by the advisor from your running list: the double week you picked on 12 November (about 205 hours, the doubled line on from your tap), Kiln to M5 and M6, Ron complete, phase 2's street budget and the rough whole street, talk's provider bake-off, people alive, hair, the first parked car. The 26 GB video folder it mentions was already deleted on 13 November with your yes, so no second tap for it. No web link: the full text is under Read it here.
detail: His order of 16 November 2026

Built by the advisor on Sunday 15 November from the running list, the builder's reports and the week's audit facts; adopted by his tap on his page. Runs from that tap to Monday 23 November 2026, 13:00 Swiss time.

The double week (his picks of 12 Nov): about 170% of a normal week, so about 205 main-line hours. The doubled line runs from 0 to 95% between Monday 13:00 and Wednesday 15:00; he presses the spare reset at the watchdog's 93% alert; then 0 to 90% by Monday 23 Nov 07:00. Unreal and the card never idle, six helpers carry the non-Unreal work, nights included.

n16-1 Kiln, clothing. Its share is set by his answer to the advisor's evaluation on Monday 07:40; held here at about 23%, front-loaded (about 35% Monday to Wednesday). Also: the parity list against Marvelous beside M7's count, FoldCraft's solver read and reused where it helps, the code-search test (two rounds with it, two without), and Kiln's disk use bounded on F:. Done: M5 and M6 met with the held-back result, and a renewal recommendation by Tuesday 24 Nov. 46 h, 23%.

n16-2 Ron as one complete person (from n09-5): his donkey jacket and trousers from the breadth set, the office exit, his routine and talk. Done: on his page with the cost table, batched with Tom's look. 10 h, 5%.

n16-3 Phase 2's street budget and scale test (time and card memory per view at a district's size; method note first), then the rough whole street with routes and doors the tester walks. Card memory's last measure (n09-3) is taken at that scale. Done: budgets measured in a packaged walk; the rough street's frame on his page at its gate. 40 h, 20%.
n16-4 The street's checks (width, kit reuse, the street's ends) and Flemish bond with burnt headers, before the corner is copied. Done: passed packaged. 10 h, 5%.
n16-5 The corner's finish copied along the street from the shopfront and slate-roof skills, each repeat costed against the first. Done: passed packaged; cost per front on the scoreboard. 15 h, 7%.

n16-6 Talk made provider-neutral, then the bake-off: Sonnet 5.5 first, then Google's and OpenAI's small models, one open model on a fast host, and one local model on his card for small talk. Then the talk quality loop, inside the day's API ceiling. Done: one recommendation on his page with first-sound times, invented details and cost per played hour. 12 h, 6%.

n16-7 People alive (from n09-8): the CMU moves through Unreal's retargeter after their review, plus idle variety and look-at on the street's walkers. Done: a packaged film passed by a fresh reviewer. 10 h, 5%.

n16-8 Hair (from n09-7): Loomwright's hair loop, capped at 8 h, with our capture fault fixed first, on Tom's crown and Darren's curls, against today's strands. Done: a verdict with renders that rides with the people looks. 8 h, 4%.
n16-9 Parked cars: the hatchback first (after his silhouette answer), by the cheapest route that passes. Done: one car passed packaged, its hours costed for the other three. 12 h, 6%.
n16-10 Efficiency and safety:
same-day packaged verdicts wherever the night walk isn't needed;
quiet starts rarer or cheaper;
the model, C:-root and output-path guards each shown firing;
the doubled line on with his tap, and the reset time recorded when the meter drops after his press;

Done: before and after in Monday's numbers. 6 h, 3%.
n16-11 Numbers from the games' files (from n09-12): UE4SS once per game, licence first, never beside Unreal. Done: the budget table. 3 h, 1%.

sections.name: Most hourly starts only find there is nothing to do, yet each pays for a full start (US$15.83 of today's US$26.12). A small check can end those starts before they cost anything. Switch it on?
sections.recommendation: Yes: about US$10 to 12 saved a day, US$50 to 80 a week. Your messages are never touched; only the hourly task's idle starts end early, and working starts run as now. If the check fails in any way, the start simply runs as it does today. It is the same kind of switch as the end-of-turn check you allowed on 11 November. The first real starts after it is on are measured and reported.
detail: What it is: a prompt-submit hook in the project's settings that runs the hourly gate before the model is called; a WAIT ends the run at once (Claude Code's hooks documentation, read 15 Nov). Built and self-tested; not switched on. Advisor's efficiency review of 15 Nov 19:46.
